sections.explanation: Validates combinations up front: a What-if must be a single on-request Prediction, Series only for Predictions and never for Track steps or end-of-task runs, Track steps must use an allowed kind, a candidate file not yet used, and a `why`. Track steps are forced non-Quick. It then checks file size, the agent-task queue, and preflights sandbox and toolchain before the agent spends effort. The returned payload carries the system prompt, numbered source and the JSON Schema produced by `z.toJSONSchema`.

sections.title: submit: single Workout path
sections.explanation: Opening the sandbox happens before counting a submission, because a missing sandbox is not the agent's fault. Each submission increments the count; `reject` deletes the generation and records `not-verified` spend once `MAX_ATTEMPTS` is reached. Schema shape is checked, then semantic checks, then the Verified gate in the sandbox. The agent-task queue is rechecked before saving because it may have filled meanwhile, and Track steps are appended on success.

sections.title: submitSeries
sections.explanation: For a Prediction Series, each submission contributes questions up to the number still needed; each is schema-checked, checked for overlap with already-kept questions, and verified separately. Verified questions are kept across submissions. The Series is saved together, under one series id, once all are in or submissions run out with at least one kept.

sections.title: list, close and queue check
sections.explanation: `list` summarises queued Workouts, normalising the legacy `fiutsu`/`kintsugi` generator names. `close` disposes the sandbox. `#checkAgentTaskQueue` refuses when agent-task Workouts already fill the cap or the same file already has one queued.

sections.title: Sandbox and environment helpers
sections.explanation: `#openSandbox` memoises a single canary-verified sandbox for the server's lifetime and never allows unsandboxed mode, so an agent cannot switch isolation off. On failure it clears the memo so a later call can retry, for example after the user installs a missing dependency. `#configEnv` and `#now` are injectable for tests.

src/agent/install.ts.overview: Implements `fiu agent install claude` and `uninstall`: writes the Fiu skill, the `/fiu-drill` and `/fiu-atlas` commands, an optional end-of-task instruction block, and registers the MCP server through the `claude` CLI. It supports user-level and per-project installs, refuses to modify git-tracked files, and cleans up installs made under the project's former names. Part of tour step 15's agent setup.

sections.title: Options, report and errors
sections.explanation: `InstallScope` distinguishes a user-wide install from a per-repository one. `runClaude` is injectable and returns undefined when the `claude` binary is missing, letting the report carry a manual command instead. `TrackedFileError` enforces the rule that Fiu never modifies tracked files.

sections.title: Install targets per scope
sections.explanation: `targets` maps a scope to file locations. User scope writes under `~/.claude` and registers MCP at user scope. Project scope writes under the repo's `.claude`, uses `CLAUDE.local.md` for the end-of-task block, and registers MCP at `local` scope, because `project` would write a tracked `.mcp.json`.

sections.title: installClaude
sections.explanation: Removes any legacy install, then writes the skill and commands; each write is guarded against tracked files and, for project scope, added to the git exclude list. The end-of-task block is added or removed according to `afterTasks`. The MCP server is removed then re-added so a moved Fiu binary is picked up; failure yields a shell-quoted manual command.

sections.title: uninstallClaude
sections.explanation: Removes only files carrying Fiu's version stamp, the now-empty skill directory, and the marked block in the memory file, then unregisters the MCP server. This keeps uninstall symmetric with install and safe around user-edited files.

sections.title: Version detection
sections.explanation: `installedVersion` reads the stamp from the user and project skill files and returns the oldest, which mcp.ts uses for the stale-install notice. `compareVersions` does a numeric dotted comparison, treating non-numeric parts as zero.

sections.title: Legacy installs
sections.explanation: `FORMER_INSTALLS` describes what Fiutsu and Kintsugi wrote: stamps, block markers, skill directories, commands and MCP server names. `legacyAgentFiles` lists leftovers for a warning, and `removeLegacyInstall` deletes only stamped files and marked blocks, unregistering the old MCP server only when its files were found, so nobody else's registration is touched.

sections.title: Small helpers
sections.explanation: `removeBlock` cuts the marked block and tidies surrounding newlines. `updateOrDelete` removes a file left empty. `guardTracked` throws for tracked paths in project scope. `runClaudeCli` uses `reject: false`, where a missing binary shows up as an undefined exit code. `shellWord` quotes only when needed.

src/agent/texts.ts.overview: All the text Fiu gives a coding agent: the MCP server instructions, each tool's description, the skill markdown, the slash-command files and the opt-in end-of-task block. The rules for using the tools live once in the server instructions, which every MCP client receives, while the skill carries only the workflow. mcp.ts and install.ts (tour step 15) import these.

sections.title: Server instructions
sections.explanation: `SERVER_INSTRUCTIONS` explains the four Workout kinds and that each is Verified, then gives step-by-step procedures for creating a Drill (including Katas, Predictions, Series, Diagnoses and What-ifs), building a Track, and building the Atlas. It closes with a guardrail: Workouts under `.fiu/` belong to the user, so the agent should coach with hints rather than solve them.

sections.title: Tool descriptions
sections.explanation: Short descriptions for each MCP tool, stating inputs, what is returned, and the meaning of each status (`saved`, `rejected`, `not-worth-practicing`, `not-enough`, `up-to-date`). They are terse because the detailed rules are already in the server instructions.

sections.title: Version stamp and skill
sections.explanation: `stamp` embeds the Fiu version as an HTML comment, and `STAMP_PATTERN` reads it back so install.ts can identify Fiu-written files and detect stale installs. `skillMarkdown` is the Claude skill: how to choose a target (using `search_atlas` for goals), delegate generation to a subagent, and report outcomes without spoiling the answer, plus parallel workflows for Tracks and the Atlas.

sections.title: Slash commands and end-of-task block
sections.explanation: `commandMarkdown` and `atlasCommandMarkdown` generate the `/fiu-drill` and `/fiu-atlas` command files that forward `$ARGUMENTS` to the skill. `afterTasksBlock`, wrapped in `BLOCK_BEGIN`/`BLOCK_END` markers so it can be removed exactly, tells the agent to create a quick Drill with `afterTask: true` after logic-changing tasks and to carry on when Fiu says the queue is full.

src/atlas/agent.ts.overview: Agent-mode Atlas tools: prepare_atlas hands the agent the next pending folder to describe, and submit_atlas checks and saves its entries.

src/atlas/render.ts.overview: Renders the Atlas view (folders, files, key functions, and per-file links) as indented terminal text or a Markdown document for `fiu atlas`.

src/atlas/search.ts.overview: Local, free stem-based search of the Atlas that ranks files and symbols against a goal, weighting name matches over entry matches and favouring unpractised code.

src/languages/paths.ts.overview: Path filter that excludes tests and generated or vendored code from what is considered drillable source.

src/background/log.ts.overview: Append-only JSON-lines log of what `fiu refill` did with each commit, with readers and a summary of unseen failures for the user.

src/commands/cost.ts.overview: Implements `fiu cost`: aggregates recorded API spend from Workouts and Attempts into monthly and per-model cost reports.

src/commands/track.ts.overview: Implements `fiu track` listing and continuation: formats Track progress and resumes the next unfinished Workout of a Track through train.

src/cost/prices.ts.overview: Built-in per-model token price table with a zod schema and a lookup helper used for cost estimation.

src/cost/usage.ts.overview: Normalizes LLM token usage, merges it by model, and estimates and formats the USD cost of generation calls.

src/explore/tracks.ts.overview: Persists and loads Tracks (ordered sequences of Workouts) in the workspace, generates track ids, and computes progress through a Track.

src/legacy.ts.overview: One-time migration from the project's former names (Fiutsu, Kintsugi): moves user config, the repository workspace, and the post-commit hook to Fiu's names.

src/map/render.ts.overview: Renders the text output of `fiu map` (practice coverage per file) and `fiu stats` (answer accuracy, calibration, and Blind Spots).

src/runner/background.ts.overview: Runs the user's own slow command (`fiu quick --while`) in the background in its own process group, logging output and reporting its result and duration.

src/sharing/git.ts.overview: Thin git plumbing wrappers for the shared-Workouts branch: fetching, reading trees and blobs, hashing, committing with a custom tree, and pushing.

src/commands/init.ts.overview: Implements `fiu init`: idempotently creates the .fiu workspace, excludes it from git, validates existing config, and checks that an OS sandbox works.
